macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Asian stocks fall as tech sell-off deepens ahead of U.S. midterms
items.summary: MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 1.4%, led by declines of up to 4.1% in South Korea and 3.6% in Taiwan. U.S. stock futures also weakened as investors awaited midterm-election results and Friday’s employment report.

items.title: U.S. futures slip as markets brace for midterm-election uncertainty
items.summary: Dow futures fell about 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures declined roughly 0.1%; Nasdaq futures were little changed. Investors are also focused on inflation, energy prices and the possibility of a December Federal Reserve rate hike, with CME FedWatch indicating a 72% probability of a 25-basis-point increase.

items.title: RBA raises interest rate to near two-decade high
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia increased its cash-rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85% in a split 6–3 decision, citing persistent inflation pressures. The Australian dollar weakened modestly despite Australian shares rising.

items.title: Apple shares slide after margin warning and weaker services outlook
items.summary: Apple shares fell about 3% in extended trading after the company forecast lower holiday-quarter gross margins because of rising memory-chip costs and projected services growth below Wall Street expectations, despite beating quarterly estimates.

items.title: Marvell to acquire Lumentum in $115 billion deal
items.summary: Marvell announced an agreement to acquire Lumentum for approximately $115 billion, adding to intense consolidation across the semiconductor and artificial-intelligence infrastructure sectors.

items.title: Palantir falls despite earnings and revenue beat
items.summary: Palantir shares dropped more than 3% in after-hours trading even though the company exceeded Wall Street’s third-quarter earnings and revenue expectations, reflecting continued investor concern over elevated technology valuations.

items.title: Oil rebounds after steep Monday decline
items.summary: Brent crude rose about 0.4%–0.5% to roughly $105.20 a barrel after falling more than 7% on Monday. Markets continued to assess U.S.–Iran peace efforts and renewed risks to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Investors prepare for major earnings slate
items.summary: AMD, Amgen, Shopify, Pfizer and other companies were scheduled to report results, giving investors additional guidance on technology demand, healthcare, consumer spending and corporate margins amid heightened market volatility.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $77,000 amid Binance-hack fallout
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $76,500–$76,800, down roughly 2.2% over 24 hours, while Ethereum, BNB and Solana also declined. The market remained pressured by ETF outflows, leverage liquidations and continuing concerns over the reported $6.3 billion Binance breach.[1][5]

items.title: Crypto market loses $176 million in liquidations
items.summary: The global crypto market capitalization fell about 0.7% to $2.678 trillion, with approximately $176 million in leveraged positions liquidated during the past 24 hours.[5]

items.title: Stolen Binance funds reportedly frozen or seized
items.summary: Elliptic reported that approximately $2.85 billion of funds linked to the Binance hack had been frozen or seized, while Binance said it had restored or recovered about 95% of affected assets.[1][5]

items.title: New Jersey drops Coinbase staking case
items.summary: New Jersey reportedly withdrew its lawsuit against Coinbase over staking and lifted the associated cease-and-desist order, removing a significant state-level regulatory obstacle for the exchange.[2][5]

items.title: CFTC advances digital-asset regulatory proposal
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission sent a cryptocurrency rule proposal to the White House for review as officials continue developing a digital-asset regulatory framework.[6]

items.title: NEAR governance approves lower token issuance ceiling
items.summary: NEAR’s House of Stake approved HSP-029, reducing the network’s maximum annual issuance rate from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.[4]

items.title: Consensys launches institutional cross-ledger settlement stack
items.summary: Consensys introduced infrastructure designed to let banks route and settle transactions across independent ledgers without transferring the underlying assets between networks.[4]

items.title: XRP payment volume surges
items.summary: XRP Ledger payment volume reportedly increased from about 229 million XRP to 1.33 billion XRP within 24 hours, although XRP’s price remained under pressure.[9]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5, positioning it for agentic coding and knowledge work, alongside the faster Claude Haiku 5.5 for high-volume tasks such as summarization, subagents, and browser use. Anthropic says Opus 5.5 costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 on Chinese AI accelerators
items.summary: Meituan released LongCat-2.5, described as a 1.6-trillion-parameter multimodal model designed for long-horizon autonomous coding. The system was reportedly trained entirely on domestically produced Chinese AI accelerators, though its benchmark claims still await independent verification.

items.title: Anthropic discloses rising AI automation in research and development
items.summary: Anthropic’s IPO filing reportedly says the company is considering human review requirements for parts of its AI research process. A related internal measure classified more than 26% of its AI research tasks as predominantly completed by AI with human monitoring by August 2026.

items.title: Anthropic warns that AI-driven research acceleration may be approaching a major milestone
items.summary: Anthropic said future models may imminently meet its internal definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI, a threshold related to recursive self-improvement. The company said its current models have not officially crossed that threshold and that human supervision remains necessary.

items.title: Tencent launches Hunyuan Research Agent 2.0
items.summary: Tencent introduced Hunyuan Research Agent 2.0, which it says can create reusable scientific tools rather than only answer individual research problems. Associated releases include protein models, inference code, technical reports, and a quantum error-correction code submitted to a competition leaderboard.

items.title: Trajectory raises $45 million to democratize AI model post-training
items.summary: AI startup Trajectory raised a $45 million Series A at a reported $300 million valuation. The company is developing tools intended to let organizations customize and post-train AI systems without depending on specialized external engineering teams.

items.title: AI infrastructure constraints expected to persist through 2027
items.summary: Industry analysis cited by IT News expects shortages of power, memory, and chip-packaging capacity to constrain AI infrastructure through 2027 as use of AI agents increases. The trend highlights continuing bottlenecks beyond model development, particularly in data-center supply and deployment capacity.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Thief: The Dark Project Remastered launches December 3
items.summary: Nightdive Studios announced a December 3, 2026 release for the remaster of the classic stealth game. It will launch on PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and PC with a new campaign created by the team behind The Black Parade.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero surpasses 4 million sales
items.summary: S-GAME says Phantom Blade Zero sold more than four million copies during its first 72 hours. The action RPG launched digitally on October 29 for PC and PlayStation 5.

items.title: Gravhounds becomes November’s first Xbox Game Pass day-one release
items.summary: The co-op action-builder Gravhounds entered Game Preview on November 2 and became the first day-one Xbox Game Pass addition of the month. It is available on Xbox Series X|S, PC, and Xbox Cloud Gaming.

items.title: Bend Studio reportedly targeting 2027 reveal and release
items.summary: Sony-owned Bend Studio is reportedly preparing a third-person co-op game that could be revealed and released in 2027. Neither Sony nor the studio has officially announced the project.

items.title: Project Takedown advances as Indian studio’s flagship project
items.summary: Shortgun Games described Project Takedown as a single-player, story-driven third-person shooter in development for PC and console. The studio also discussed investor backing from Indian actor Mahesh Babu and the growth of India’s game-development sector.

items.title: Nintendo awarded $4.5 million in piracy case
items.summary: A Washington federal judge reportedly entered a $4.5 million default judgment against a Reddit moderator accused of distributing unauthorized Nintendo Switch game copies.

items.title: GTA VI’s expected November launch draws major industry attention
items.summary: Coverage highlighted the anticipated economic and cultural impact of Grand Theft Auto VI, including possible effects on streaming, music, social media, consumer products, and travel. Reports list a November 19, 2026 release date, though the supplied coverage varies in the level of official confirmation.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Marvell agrees to acquire Lumentum in major semiconductor deal
items.summary: Marvell Technology announced plans to acquire optical-components maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at roughly $115 billion, expanding its position in data-center connectivity and networking hardware.[4]

items.title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher backlash
items.summary: Meta postponed changes to its business terms following criticism over provisions that could have enabled broader scraping of news websites.[6]

items.title: European supermarkets report disruptions linked to apparent cyberattacks
items.summary: Supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia experienced refrigeration-system disruptions that were apparently caused by cyberattacks, according to reports summarized by the Associated Press.[3]

items.title: FBI attributes historic Binance crypto theft to North Korean hackers
items.summary: The FBI said North Korean hackers orchestrated the theft of billions of dollars from Binance, describing it as the largest crypto heist in history.[3]

items.title: GMO Internet apologizes for security breaches
items.summary: Japan’s GMO Internet Group apologized after unauthorized access to its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service caused information leaks and unrecognized transactions affecting multiple businesses.[3]

items.title: Apple reports stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue
items.summary: Apple posted quarterly revenue above expectations, helped by improving iPhone sales, while its stock performance and comparatively cautious technology spending continued to draw investor attention.[4]
